objective: Reduce perceived and actual IGPAT first-frame startup and swipe latency on Android/Web using the installed Expo SDK 57 video system; preserve private media, sponsored Reels, audio mixing, Quick Edit and consolidated OTA hold.
productionBaselineEvidence: Reconciled 2026-11-11 GitHub main at 538f94d0305548ebe94425fded526bca7c02d048 including permanent ads lock. All six pre-existing touched files verified byte-identical between old scope baseline and latest main before copying. No actual device test/production OTA verified. DEV branch only.
chosenApproach: Create one ahead VideoPlayer but mount VideoView only for the active reel. Measure native playback startup when the first frame actually renders rather than at playingChange, with a UI placeholder and direct user-gesture recovery for blocked/stalled autoplay. Lower normal-network initial buffer to 0.75s and keep conservative 1.5s buffer for weak-network/Data Saver. Render two feed cells up front. Apply to Android and Web only. For the following rows, sign the immediately next video separately and batch all later private Storage paths in one request, recovering missing paths with two bounded concurrent individual signs and publishing updates in a single React batch. Bound first and background Storage waits to 9s. On the very first feed request, render the already-authorized RPC metadata immediately while the first private media link is signed; preserve changes to visible reactions/counts and the user's swipe index when signing resolves. Deliver successful batch links early even if a missing-path fallback is slow. For framing: Android/inline previews already use contain; restore WEB default from cover to contain, make new Quick Edit default contain, stop Auto Improve from silently switching into cropped 9:16, preserve explicitly chosen crop-to-fill and rotation, change Home IGPAT preview to contain, and avoid zoomed browser camera preview.
selectionRationale: Expo documentation supports preloading a player without a VideoView and onFirstFrameRender. Avoids simultaneous offscreen surfaces and background decoding pressure without replacing expo-video or rearchitecting signed URLs. Keeps existing progressive first-item signing and next organic clip preload.
acceptanceChecks: First video shows immediate loading state and clears it only after actual first frame, not merely player playing event
Healthy networks start at 0.75 second minimum buffer while weak network uses existing 1.5s
One next organic video preloads without rendering an offscreen video surface; no eager ad video preloading
Offscreen video never plays; on swipe back active video mounts its view
After 3 seconds without first frame the active clip offers direct tap-to-play recovery; no automatic unbounded request retry
Preserve signed private Supabase URLs and 8 minute account-scoped warm feed; do not persist URLs
Preserve Reels ad cadence, interactive gestures, web Quick Edit and PTT-compatible audioMixingMode
Focused Node regression plus TypeScript/CI gate; skipped real Android device test remains unverified
Existing Nov10 fast-start regression may be run as additional unchanged coverage, but only this change's new test is declared in the changed-test gate.
Batch signing response may arrive out of order; URL access must map by verified exact path
Unrelated/mismatched signed paths are ignored; no cross-account URL adoption or persistence
Duplicate paths are signed once; missing/permission-denied rows become retryable, not permanently loading
On navigation/logout newer feed generation cancels remaining fallback and discards stale URLs
At most two fallback individual requests at a time; one list update per signing stage, not one per item
Existing Nov10 signing test is updated rather than weakened/deleted
RPC completion paints authorized feed rows before first private URL signing completes; no placeholders remain indefinitely on returned errors
First URL response does not reset the viewer to item zero after the user swipes
User reaction/comment count changes while signing remain intact after the first URL returns
Batch successes publish before a slow partial fallback without waiting for its missing paths
IGPAT Android and web default rendering preserves the original video aspect ratio (contain; letterbox rather than crop)
Home and inline IGPAT previews also show the full video without cover zoom
Quick Edit defaults to contain; Auto Improve never changes framing to cover by itself
Manual CROP TO FILL remains available to the creator and serializes/parses correctly
Legacy IGPAT metadata with no content_fit is treated as contain; explicitly saved cover remains respected
Web camera preview is not implicitly cropped by CSS objectFit cover
New focused regression checks prove contain defaults and manual crop compatibility
preserveBehaviors: Canonical BUKLOD navigation and legacy /reels alias
Supabase RLS and 20 minute signed media URLs
Native sponsored Reel slides and existing Google IMA branch
Data Saver/weak signal next preloading restrictions
Quick Edit trim/rotation/speed, temporary 2x long press and mute/audio mixing
No new native package, backend schema, paid encoding, cloud provider or direct production publish
Publisher-initiated crop-to-fill Quick Edit, trim, rotation and cover-frame metadata remain opt-in
riskAreas: First frame callback timing on Android SurfaceView
Fast swipe View mounting and pause/reuse
Supabase Storage batch response ordering and partial failures
early feed interaction while private URL signing remains pending
alternativeApproaches: Adopt new player or CDN/transcoding (rejected: new cost, backend and native upgrade)
Preload the entire feed (rejected: memory/data/permissions risk)
Play all adjacent videos offscreen (rejected: excessive decoder/audio usage)
Mount native VideoView only for active item while preloading VideoPlayer (selected)
Continue per-row signing of all 16 clips and 15 React state updates (rejected: network and render contention)
Force cover to occupy 9:16 viewport (rejected: crops and zooms landscape and nonstandard aspect videos)
Remove crop-to-fill control entirely (rejected: breaks author-intentional edits)
